source_pins.finding: Tip-of-tree Page.startScreencast is experimental and emits compressed images through Page.screencastFrame; the frame event carries an integer sessionId documented as the frame number and is paired with screencastFrameAck.

source_pins.source: Chrome DevTools Protocol official Page domain
source_pins.finding: Page.startScreencast can bound image format/quality/width/height and everyNthFrame, giving a direct source for browser/rendered capture without importing a full automation framework.

source_pins.source: Chrome DevTools Protocol official DOMSnapshot domain
source_pins.finding: DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot returns a flattened document snapshot including DOM tree, iframes/template/imported documents, layout and selected computed-style data; DocumentSnapshot exposes frameId, providing a structural browser channel with frame provenance.

source_pins.source: Chrome DevTools Protocol official Target domain
source_pins.finding: Target.attachToTarget(targetId, flatten=true) returns a string Target.SessionID used to route commands in flat mode, providing a target/session anchor for rendered and structural operations.

source_pins.source: Chrome DevTools Protocol official version guidance
source_pins.finding: Tip-of-tree changes frequently and has no guaranteed backwards compatibility; stable 1.3 is a much smaller Chrome-64-era subset and does not expose Page.startScreencast. Any F2 adapter must bind browser/protocol identity instead of assuming a timeless CDP ABI.

critical_identity_finding: CDP has two semantically different fields that can both look like session identity: Target.SessionID is a string debugging-session identifier, while Page.screencastFrame.sessionId is an integer frame number. F2 must name them separately (for example cdp_target_session_id and cdp_screencast_frame_id) to avoid provenance aliasing.
result: A thin CDP adapter is source-plausible for the already-required browser/rendered and browser/structural Perception Fabric channels. One attached target/session can issue Page and DOMSnapshot commands, while target/frame identities can be carried as non-authoritative provenance. This does not establish temporal simultaneity, runtime performance, browser-version compatibility, or F2 integration acceptance.
counterhypotheses: Screencast and DOM snapshot observations may refer to measurably different page states under fast mutation; shared target/session identity is not proof of simultaneity.
Experimental Page.startScreencast may change or disappear across Chromium revisions and may be less stable than periodic Page.captureScreenshot.
DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot may be too heavy for the desired structural cadence; a thinner DOM/accessibility projection could be cheaper.
A browser automation framework could handle compatibility/reconnect semantics more robustly, but would add dependency and control-plane weight that may duplicate F2 authority/routing.
next_discriminator: Acquire a separate E2_ARCHITECTURE_MAPPED claim and map the smallest CDP BrowserCaptureAdapter contract against current F2 capture/temporal/local-acceptance source, explicitly testing identity separation, navigation/reconnect, dual-channel skew semantics, and dependency weight before any build candidate.
